sources.scope: Selected actual university description through search read: scale-leaved conical tree with flattened horizontal sprays, small thin overlapping cone scales, small resinous glands. No cultivar-specific dimensions or growth rates fitted.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected institutional botanical description through web retrieval; local HTML cached

findings.shape: A detailed selected arborvitae shoot branches into flattened fan-like horizontal sprays with small overlapping scale-leaf surfaces and selected small elongated seed cones with thin woody scale cues. This is a leafy organ study rather than a whole mature tree.
findings.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
findings.movement: Same retained woody axes, rachises, leaves and reproductive surfaces during small authored external deflection. Root/support position and scale remain anchored. Timing and angles are qualitative; there is no wind/elasticity solver, physiological simulation or measured biomechanics. Complete germination, organ emergence and seed-to-adult development are unavailable; no resizing of a ready mature plant.
findings.evidenceScope: Selected actual university description through search read: scale-leaved conical tree with flattened horizontal sprays, small thin overlapping cone scales, small resinous glands. No cultivar-specific dimensions or growth rates fitted.
corrections: Replaced the repeated whole conifer with a selected flattened compound leafy spray.
Corrected appressed scale orientation and overlap, and moved cones from the main shoot to attached terminal short branches.
Replaced generic spiral cone fans with ten selected paired thin oblong scale surfaces; added separate foliage and reproductive camera directions.
findings.residual: Only a selected shoot is reconstructed. Sprays still have visibly regular saw-toothed edges and gaps; resin glands, fine facial/lateral scale anatomy, wood/cuticle optics and natural proportions are incomplete. The retained photo shows immature green cones whereas the selected reconstruction illustrates a woody mature form; it is not a pixel/colour match to that stage. Cone opening and whole-tree development are unavailable.
